title: When puberty is late enough to evaluate
lead: Evaluate no breast development by age 13, no menarche by age 15, or no testicular enlargement by age 14.
lines: Those ages start the workup. They are not themselves a diagnosis.
Constitutional delay is a diagnosis of exclusion after the exam, the growth curve, and the indicated labs.
A girl who started breasts and has no period three years later is also late, even if she is not yet 15.
miss: Reassuring a 15-year-old with no periods because a cousin was a late bloomer.
diagramAlt: When to evaluate puberty. Girl: no breast by 13, no menses by 15 Boy: testes under 4 mL at 14 Bone age first. High FSH = gonadal failure

source.name: StatPearls. Delayed Puberty.
source.says: These sex hormones are responsible for the physical signs of puberty; in females, the first sign of true puberty is breast development (thelarche), whereas in males it is testicular enlargement (testicular volume ≥4 mL or testicular length >2.5 cm).

title: Ambiguous genitalia can be salt-wasting disease
lead: A newborn with atypical genitalia is evaluated for salt-wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia before the baby goes home.
lines: A virilized or atypical newborn is evaluated for 21-hydroxylase deficiency before anyone assigns a sex or sends the infant home.
Salt-wasting disease is part of that guideline's clinical management, not a reassurance visit.
The infant who is ill is treated, not observed until a karyotype result returns.
In weeks 1 to 3 the sodium falls and the potassium rises, often above 6. 17-hydroxyprogesterone is very high. Give hydrocortisone and saline, then fludrocortisone.
miss: Discharging a virilized newborn with no plan for salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency.
diagramAlt: Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase. Week 1–3: Na low, K over 6 17-hydroxyprogesterone very high Hydrocortisone + saline, then fludrocortisone

source.name: Endocrine Society guideline. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.
source.says: This is the Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline for the management of congenital adrenal hyperplasia caused by steroid 21-hydroxylase deficiency, including the salt-wasting form.

title: Turner syndrome is followed for the aorta and the growth
lead: A girl with Turner syndrome gets blood-pressure checks, aortic imaging, and a growth conversation. The karyotype is not the end of the visit.
lines: Coarctation and a bicuspid valve are what you listen and image for.
The kidneys are imaged once.
Estrogen is replaced at the time of puberty, with a specialist, because the streak gonads will not produce it.
miss: Measuring height once and never taking a blood pressure in the legs.

source.name: Clinical practice guidelines for the care of girls and women with Turner syndrome.
source.says: Girls and women with Turner syndrome need cardiac evaluation for coarctation and a bicuspid aortic valve, including an arm and a leg blood pressure.

title: Klinefelter syndrome is treated as hypogonadism
lead: Men with Klinefelter syndrome and low testosterone are offered testosterone replacement. The infertility is a separate conversation and is not fixed by the gel.
lines: Breast tissue is examined because the cancer risk is higher.
Learning differences are supported. They are not the reason to withhold hormone treatment.
Testosterone treats the hypogonadism. It does not restore sperm. Breast cancer risk is higher than in other men.
Small firm testes, tall stature, azoospermia, and gynecomastia. Testosterone is low and LH and FSH are high.
miss: Telling the patient testosterone will restore sperm.

source.name: StatPearls. Klinefelter Syndrome.
source.says: Affected individuals often present with tall stature, small testes, gynecomastia, and azoospermia.

title: DiGeorge is calcium, infection, and the heart
lead: A newborn with DiGeorge features gets a calcium, an immune evaluation, and a heart evaluation. The low calcium can be the first seizure.
lines: Irradiated blood is used if a transfusion is needed and the immune defect is not yet clear.
Live vaccines wait until the immune status is known.
The face and the outflow murmur are the clues to order those tests.
Third pouch: inferior parathyroids and thymus. Fourth pouch: superior parathyroids.
Ionized calcium can fall in the first days of life. A neonatal seizure here is hypocalcemia until the lab returns.
miss: Treating a neonatal seizure with an antiseizure drug and never checking the calcium.

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroanatomy, Neural Crest.
source.says: DiGeorge features in a newborn are a reason to check calcium, immune function, and the heart. A hypocalcemic seizure can be the first sign.

title: TTP is not a platelet order
lead: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura is a medical emergency treated with plasma exchange. Platelets are for life-threatening bleeding, not for the number.
lines: High clinical suspicion: draw ADAMTS13 before any plasma exchange or blood product.
Then start therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids without waiting for the ADAMTS13 result.
The ISTH treatment guideline strongly recommends adding corticosteroids to plasma exchange for a first episode or a relapse.
Caplacizumab is a conditional addition in the treatment guideline. It is not a reason to delay plasma exchange.
miss: Waiting for the ADAMTS13 result before plasma exchange when the clinical suspicion is already high.
diagramAlt: TTP versus ITP. TTP: schistocytes, hemolysis, exchange now ITP: isolated low platelets, no fragments Platelets in TTP only for life-threatening bleed

source.name: ISTH guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.
source.says: When suspicion is high, draw ADAMTS13 before plasma exchange, then start plasma exchange and corticosteroids without waiting for the result. The treatment guideline strongly recommends corticosteroids added to plasma exchange for a first episode or a relapse.

title: Febrile neutropenia does not wait for the culture
lead: Fever with an absolute neutrophil count under 500 needs an antipseudomonal antibiotic within an hour of recognition.
lines: Fever plus neutropenia is treated at once with broad empiric antibiotics. Do not wait for a culture to grow.
The IDSA 2010 update states that immediate empiric therapy has not changed: cover gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens.
Risk stratification decides the setting. It does not delay the first dose.
A narrow oral drug chosen before that first broad dose is the miss.
miss: Waiting for the culture result before the first broad antibiotic dose.

source.name: IDSA 2010 update. Antimicrobial agents in neutropenic patients with cancer.
source.says: All patients who present with fever and neutropenia should be treated swiftly and broadly with empiric antibiotics. Immediate treatment is the standing recommendation of this guideline.

title: Acute chest syndrome is more than pain medicine
lead: Acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease is a new infiltrate with chest pain, fever, or hypoxia. Incentive spirometry prevents it, and severe disease is an exchange-transfusion conversation.
lines: Antibiotics cover community pneumonia while you treat the sickle crisis.
Simple transfusion is for a drop in hemoglobin. Exchange is for the severe respiratory failure.
Pain control that lets the patient take deep breaths is part of the prevention.
Exchange transfusion for severe acute chest or acute stroke. Simple transfusion is for symptomatic anemia. Hydroxyurea is prevention, not today's stroke drug.
miss: Discharging a hypoxic sickle-cell patient with oral opioids and no film.

source.name: BSH guideline on acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease.
source.says: Incentive spirometry is used on sickle-cell pain admissions, and a new infiltrate with hypoxia is acute chest syndrome.

title: Bleeding ITP is treated. A number alone may not be
lead: Immune thrombocytopenia is treated when there is bleeding or a procedure, not because every low number must be normalized today.
lines: ASH lists observation as a way to manage immune thrombocytopenia when bleeding is not forcing treatment.
When treatment is chosen, corticosteroids are one of the approaches the guideline considers.
The panel favored options that avoid drug toxicity for non–life-threatening bleeding.
Approaches named in the guideline also include IVIG, anti-D immunoglobulin, rituximab, splenectomy, and thrombopoietin receptor agonists.
miss: Transfusing platelets for a number, in a patient who is not bleeding, as the treatment of immune thrombocytopenia.
diagramAlt: TTP versus ITP. TTP: schistocytes, hemolysis, exchange now ITP: isolated low platelets, no fragments Platelets in TTP only for life-threatening bleed

source.name: ASH 2019 guidelines for immune thrombocytopenia.
source.says: Observation is a management option for ITP. When treatment is used, corticosteroids are among the listed approaches. The panel favored strategies that avoid medication side effects when bleeding is not life-threatening.

title: A hemophilia bleed gets factor, not fresh frozen plasma as the plan
lead: A joint or muscle bleed in hemophilia A is treated with factor VIII replacement. Fresh frozen plasma is not the outpatient plan.
lines: A mixing study that no longer corrects means an inhibitor.
Avoid intramuscular injections and NSAIDs.
PT is normal. PTT is long and corrects with mixing unless an inhibitor has formed.
miss: Sending a hemarthrosis home on ibuprofen.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemophilia A.
source.says: The natural history of untreated hemophilia A is marked by progressive joint damage and increased morbidity; however, advances in factor replacement therapy and prophylactic treatment have significantly improved life expectancy and quality of life.

title: Desmopressin is for type 1 von Willebrand, not type 2B
lead: Type 1 von Willebrand disease can be treated with desmopressin before a procedure. Type 2B can worsen because the abnormal multimer binds platelets.
lines: Know the subtype before the drug.
Antifibrinolytics help mucosal bleeding.
Factor replacement that contains von Willebrand factor is the alternative when desmopressin is unsafe.
vWF carries factor VIII. Mucosal bleeding with a normal platelet count is the picture. PTT prolongs only if VIII is low.
miss: Giving desmopressin to every patient with the disease name and watching the platelet count fall.
diagramAlt: Desmopressin in VWD. Type 1: desmopressin often works Type 2B: desmopressin can drop platelets Mucosal bleeding. PTT may be normal

source.name: ASH ISTH NHF WFH 2021 guidelines on von Willebrand disease.
source.says: Desmopressin is appropriate for many patients with type 1 von Willebrand disease and is not used in type 2B, where the platelet count can fall.

title: DIC is treated by treating the cause
lead: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is treated by treating the cause. Blood products are for bleeding or a procedure, not for a daily number.
lines: Treat the underlying condition. That is the cornerstone of DIC treatment in the ISTH harmonized guidance.
Transfuse platelets or plasma only for a patient who is bleeding, not for a number alone.
If thrombosis is the dominant picture, consider a therapeutic dose of heparin. Do not use that dose when bleeding risk is high.
Critically ill patients who are not bleeding should receive prophylactic unfractionated or low-molecular-weight heparin.
miss: Treating a laboratory number with plasma while the cause of the DIC is left untreated.
diagramAlt: DIC labs. Low fibrinogen, high D-dimer PT and PTT both prolong Cryoprecipitate if bleeding and fibrinogen is low

source.name: ISTH SSC guidance. Diagnosis and treatment of DIC, harmonized from three guidelines.
source.says: The cornerstone of DIC treatment is treatment of the underlying condition. Transfusion of platelets or plasma is reserved for patients who are bleeding. Therapeutic heparin is considered when thrombosis predominates, and prophylactic heparin is recommended in critically ill, non-bleeding patients.

title: Do not start warfarin alone for HIT
lead: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is treated by stopping all heparin and starting a non-heparin anticoagulant. Warfarin alone is dangerous in the acute phase.
lines: Estimate probability with the 4Ts score, not a gestalt impression.
A low-probability 4Ts score is not an indication to stop heparin and start another anticoagulant.
An intermediate or high score: stop heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant. ASH names argatroban, bivalirudin, danaparoid, fondaparinux, and a direct oral anticoagulant.
Do not start warfarin before the platelet count recovers, usually to at least 150 × 10^9/L. Early warfarin is linked to venous limb gangrene.
miss: Stopping heparin without a non-heparin anticoagulant when the 4Ts score is intermediate or high, or starting warfarin while the platelet count is still low.
diagramAlt: HIT, day 5 to 10. Platelets fall >=50% at day 5-10 With or without thrombosis Stop heparin. No warfarin before recovery

source.name: ASH 2018 guideline for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
source.says: Use the 4Ts score rather than gestalt. Do not treat empirically when the score is low. For an intermediate or high score, stop heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant. Do not start a vitamin K antagonist before the platelet count recovers, usually to at least 150 × 10^9/L.

title: Established tumor lysis with a high uric acid gets rasburicase
lead: Allopurinol prevents new uric acid. Rasburicase breaks down uric acid that is already there. A high uric acid with tumor lysis gets rasburicase if it is available.
lines: Fluids are started in everyone at risk.
Screen for G6PD deficiency before rasburicase when you can. The drug can hemolyze those patients.
The potassium is the immediate threat on the monitor.
Potassium and phosphate and uric acid rise. Calcium falls.
miss: Starting only allopurinol when the uric acid is already 14 and the potassium is 6.
diagramAlt: Tumor lysis ions. K up, phosphate up, uric acid up Calcium down (binds phosphate) Rasburicase clears uric acid already made

source.name: StatPearls. Tumor Lysis Syndrome.
source.says: Given the severe lethality of tumor lysis syndrome, identifying patients at increased risk and initiating early preventive measures are crucial.

title: Phlebotomy is the treatment of polycythemia vera
lead: Polycythemia vera is treated by phlebotomy to lower the hematocrit, plus aspirin when the diagnosis is secure and the platelets are not extreme.
lines: A high erythropoietin is not this disease. Do not phlebotomize hypoxic lung disease down to an unsafe hematocrit.
Hydroxyurea is added for high-risk patients.
Aquagenic itching is a clue, not a dermatology referral alone.
A high EPO is secondary erythrocytosis.
Do not apply that target to hypoxic lung disease.
miss: Phlebotomizing a patient with a high EPO from lung disease to a hematocrit of 40.
diagramAlt: Polycythemia vera target. JAK2. EPO is low Phlebotomy toward hematocrit <45% Do not phlebotomize hypoxic high-EPO disease

source.name: ELN revised management recommendations for myeloproliferative neoplasms.
source.says: Phlebotomy in polycythemia vera targets a hematocrit below 45%.

title: Start ATRA when the smear says promyelocytic leukemia
lead: Acute promyelocytic leukemia is treated with all-trans retinoic acid as soon as the diagnosis is suspected. Do not wait for the karyotype if the smear and the coagulopathy match.
lines: The early death is bleeding. Correct the coagulopathy.
Differentiation syndrome is fever and pulmonary infiltrates after the drug starts. It is treated, not ignored.
Auer rods and a bilobed nucleus are the smear. The translocation is between chromosomes 15 and 17.
miss: Waiting three days for cytogenetics while the fibrinogen falls.
diagramAlt: APL, do not wait. Auer rods. t(15;17) ATRA when the smear fits Bleeding is the early death. Follow fibrinogen

source.name: ELN expert-panel recommendations for acute promyelocytic leukemia.
source.says: Start all-trans retinoic acid as soon as acute promyelocytic leukemia is suspected, and follow fibrinogen because the early death is bleeding.

title: PNH with hemolysis or thrombosis gets a complement inhibitor
lead: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria with hemolysis or thrombosis is treated with a complement inhibitor. Anticoagulation alone does not stop the complement.
lines: Unusual-site thrombosis is this disease until the flow cytometry is back.
Iron is lost in the urine. Replace it if the patient is deficient. Do not assume the anemia is iron overload.
Eculizumab raises the Neisseria risk. Vaccinate.
miss: Anticoagulating a hepatic-vein thrombosis and never ordering the flow cytometry.

source.name: StatPearls. Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria.
source.says: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) is a rare disease that presents clinically with a variety of symptoms, the most prevalent of which are hemolytic anemia, hemoglobinuria, and somatic symptoms including fatigue and shortness of breath.

title: A hemolytic transfusion reaction stops the unit
lead: Fever, pain, or dark urine during a transfusion stops that unit. Do not slow it and watch.
lines: Check the identity of the patient and the bag. Clerical error is the classic cause.
Support the pressure and the urine output.
A febrile nonhemolytic reaction is a diagnosis you make after hemolysis is unlikely, not before you stop the blood.
ABO mismatch causes fever, flank pain, and hemoglobinuria during the transfusion. Stop that unit.
Keep the bag. Send it back with a fresh sample. Clerical error is the usual cause. Do not restart the same unit.
miss: Restarting the same unit after acetaminophen.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction.
source.says: Immune HTRs often occur due to mismatch or incompatibility of the patient with the donor products and are classified as acute versus delayed hemolytic reactions.

title: Either thrombolytic, inside 4.5 hours
lead: For an eligible adult within 4.5 hours, give tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg up to 25 mg, or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg up to 90 mg.
lines: Disabling deficit is the indication. A low NIHSS score does not cancel it.
Do not use advanced imaging to withhold treatment inside 4.5 hours.
Tenecteplase 0.4 mg/kg is not the dose in this window.
Check glucose and a noncontrast CT first. Hypoglycemia copies a stroke and is not treated with a thrombolytic.
miss: Waiting for an MRI, or quoting only alteplase, in a patient who is already inside the window.
diagramAlt: Inside 4.5 hours, tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg up to 25 mg or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg up to 90 mg. Blood pressure before treatment is below 185 over 110.

source.name: 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke.
source.says: The guideline endorses either tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (maximum 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (maximum 90 mg) within 4.5 hours, without advanced-imaging selection.

title: Status epilepticus: benzodiazepine first
lead: A seizure that continues, or that recurs without recovery, gets a benzodiazepine now. The second drug is not another benzodiazepine.
lines: Give IV lorazepam, or IM midazolam if there is no IV.
If it continues, give one adequate dose of fosphenytoin, valproate, or levetiracetam. Those three are equivalent as the next drug.
Do not stack small benzodiazepine doses and call that treatment.
Check glucose, then give a benzodiazepine: intravenous lorazepam or intramuscular midazolam if there is no line.

If the seizure continues, give one full dose of levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4500 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg/kg (max 1500 mg), or valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3000 mg). ESETT found them equivalent. Do not stack quarter-doses.
miss: Starting a phenytoin load while the first benzodiazepine dose was never given.
diagramAlt: Status epilepticus drugs. Glucose, then a benzodiazepine Then one full second drug Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, or valproate

source.name: Kapur et al. Randomized Trial of Three Anticonvulsant Medications for Status Epilepticus. N Engl J Med.
source.says: Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, and valproate were equivalent as the second intravenous drug after a benzodiazepine.

title: Thunderclap headache is a bleed until it is not
lead: A headache that is maximal at onset gets a noncontrast head CT now. A negative early CT does not close the question.
lines: Do the CT before the neurology consult and before a migraine cocktail.
If the CT is negative and the story is still a thunderclap in the first hours, the next test is lumbar puncture or a vascular study, based on timing and availability.
Exertion, pregnancy, a focal deficit, fever with neck stiffness, cancer, or immunosuppression also moves imaging up. A stable recurrent migraine does not.
miss: Sending the patient home because the CT was read overnight as negative and nobody asked how the headache started.

source.name: 2023 AHA/ASA guideline for aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
source.says: A thunderclap headache is imaged with noncontrast CT immediately. A negative early CT does not end the evaluation. ACEP 2019 is the emergency-department policy for the next test.

title: Dexamethasone before the meningitis antibiotic
lead: In adults with suspected pneumococcal meningitis, give dexamethasone before or with the first antibiotic dose.
lines: The point is to blunt the inflammatory burst as bacteria lyse. After the antibiotic is already in, the window is gone.
Do not delay the antibiotic for a CT if there is no indication for CT. Blood cultures, then drug, then the puncture if imaging has to come first.
Stop the steroid if the organism is not Streptococcus pneumoniae, unless another indication exists.
miss: Hanging the antibiotic, then remembering the steroid an hour later.

source.name: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Management of Bacterial Meningitis.
source.says: The IDSA adult guideline recommends dexamethasone before or with the first dose when pneumococcal meningitis is suspected. This remains the standing IDSA guideline.

title: Guillain-Barré is IVIG or exchange, not prednisone
lead: Guillain-Barré syndrome is treated with intravenous immunoglobulin or plasma exchange. Steroids do not help.
lines: IVIg 0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days if the patient cannot walk unaided and weakness began within 2 weeks. A good-practice point also allows 2 to 4 weeks.
Or plasma exchange, 12–15 L in four to five exchanges over 1 to 2 weeks, if weakness began within 4 weeks and the patient cannot walk unaided.
Do not use oral corticosteroids. A second course of IVIg for a poor prognosis is recommended against.
Use the modified Erasmus GBS Respiratory Insufficiency Score for the ventilation risk. CSF examination is valuable when the diagnosis is uncertain.
miss: Starting prednisone, or quoting a vital-capacity cutoff this guideline does not use, instead of IVIg or plasma exchange.
diagramAlt: Guillain-Barré breathing. IVIG or exchange. Not prednisone Vital capacity under 20 mL/kg: intubate window CSF: high protein, almost no cells

source.name: EAN/PNS guideline on diagnosis and treatment of Guillain-Barré syndrome.
source.says: IVIg 0.4 g/kg for 5 days is recommended within 2 weeks of onset if the patient cannot walk unaided, or plasma exchange of 12–15 L in four to five exchanges if within 4 weeks. Oral corticosteroids are recommended against. The mEGRIS score estimates the need for ventilation.

title: An acute multiple-sclerosis flare gets a steroid, not an antibiotic
lead: A new disabling multiple-sclerosis flare is treated with high-dose corticosteroids. An antibiotic does not treat a demyelinating plaque.
lines: Infection can worsen old symptoms without a new plaque. Look for it before you call every worsening a flare.
Disease-modifying therapy is the long plan and is not the same syringe as the flare steroid.
Optic neuritis is this conversation, and vision is followed.
Dissemination in time and space, plus unmatched oligoclonal bands. One lesion is not the disease.
A new disabling deficit can get high-dose steroids. The same old deficit plus a fever is infection until proved otherwise.
miss: Giving antibiotics for a sensory level and a clear urine.
diagramAlt: MS flare versus infection. New deficit: high-dose steroid Old deficit plus fever: find the infection Disease-modifying drug is a separate order

source.name: AAN practice guideline. Disease-modifying therapies for adults with multiple sclerosis.
source.says: Offer a disease-modifying therapy for relapsing multiple sclerosis. A new deficit on admission is evaluated for infection or relapse before the therapy is changed.

title: Levodopa is the most effective drug for Parkinson motor symptoms
lead: When Parkinson disease limits function, levodopa is the most effective drug for the motor symptoms. Saving it for late disease is an old idea.
lines: Carbidopa is given with it so less is lost in the periphery.
A dopamine blocker on the medication list is stopped before the diagnosis is locked.
Impulse-control problems are the agonist story. Ask about gambling and sex.
Rest tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia from nigral dopamine loss. Give hospital doses at the home clock times.
miss: Withholding levodopa for years from a patient who can no longer walk, out of fear of it wearing off.
diagramAlt: Parkinson doses in hospital. Give carbidopa-levodopa at home times No metoclopramide or haloperidol Levodopa is the strongest motor drug

source.name: StatPearls. Parkinson Disease.
source.says: PD usually presents in later life with the cardinal clinical motor features of bradykinesia, resting tremor, and rigidity, often in various combinations.

title: Absence epilepsy is ethosuximide
lead: Ethosuximide is the drug for childhood absence seizures. Carbamazepine can worsen them.
lines: There is no postictal confusion. A confused child had a different seizure.
Hyperventilation can reproduce the spell in the office.
A child who also has generalized convulsions needs a drug that covers both, which ethosuximide does not.
Ethosuximide if this is the only seizure type.
miss: Starting carbamazepine for staring spells.
diagramAlt: Absence drug. 3 Hz spike-and-wave. No postictal state Ethosuximide if absence is the only seizure Carbamazepine can worsen pure absence

source.name: StatPearls. Absence Seizure.
source.says: Absence seizures occur in multiple genetic generalized epilepsies, including childhood absence epilepsy (CAE), juvenile absence epilepsy (JAE), and juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME).

title: Carbamazepine is first for trigeminal neuralgia
lead: Trigeminal neuralgia is treated with carbamazepine. A dental extraction is not the treatment of electric pain.
lines: The shock lasts under 2 minutes, in one trigeminal division, and is triggered by touch, chewing, or a breeze.
Carbamazepine is first-line. Check sodium. A spreading rash can be Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and the drug stops.
Oxcarbazepine is the usual alternative. A dental extraction does not treat the nerve.
miss: Pulling a tooth for seconds of shock-like pain in the cheek.
diagramAlt: Trigeminal neuralgia. Seconds of shock in one branch Carbamazepine first Check sodium. Young or numb: image

source.name: AAN/EFNS practice parameter. Treatment of trigeminal neuralgia.
source.says: Carbamazepine is established as effective for pain in classical trigeminal neuralgia.

title: Stop the antipsychotic in neuroleptic malignant syndrome
lead: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is treated by stopping the dopamine blocker, cooling, and supporting the pressure. Another dose of the same drug is not the treatment of the agitation.
lines: Creatine kinase is high and the reflexes are not clonus.
A benzodiazepine can help agitation. The antipsychotic does not.
Restarting a drug later, if ever, is a specialist decision at a low dose.
Lead-pipe rigidity and high CK over days. Reflexes are reduced, not clonic.
miss: Increasing the antipsychotic because the patient is more confused.
diagramAlt: NMS versus serotonin syndrome. NMS: lead-pipe, high CK, days Serotonin: clonus, hours, two drugs Stop the offending drug in both

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
source.says: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is a life-threatening syndrome associated with the use of dopamine-receptor antagonist medications or with the rapid withdrawal of dopaminergic medications.

title: Stop the serotonergic drugs
lead: Serotonin syndrome is treated by stopping the serotonergic drugs and giving a benzodiazepine for agitation. Cyproheptadine is the antidote when supportive care is not enough.
lines: Clonus is the sign that separates it from neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
It starts in hours, so today's new prescription is the cause.
Clonus and hyperreflexia within hours of an SSRI plus an MAOI, linezolid, tramadol, or a triptan. Stop both drugs on that shift.
A benzodiazepine treats the agitation. Cyproheptadine is the antagonist if support is not enough. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is rigidity over days, not clonus.
miss: Adding linezolid to an SSRI and treating the shivering as influenza.
diagramAlt: NMS versus serotonin syndrome. NMS: lead-pipe, high CK, days Serotonin: clonus, hours, two drugs Stop the offending drug in both

source.name: StatPearls. Serotonin Syndrome.
source.says: Treatment for serotonin syndrome involves discontinuing the offending medications and providing supportive care.

title: A high lithium level is held, and severe toxicity is dialyzed
lead: Hold lithium and check the level when tremor, confusion, or a drug interaction appears. Severe neurotoxicity or a very high level is dialyzed.
lines: Hold lithium when toxicity is suspected and send a level timed after distribution, not in the first hours.
EXTRIP recommends extracorporeal treatment for severe lithium poisoning.
Intravenous saline treats volume loss. It does not replace dialysis when neurotoxicity is severe.
Chronic use can cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. That is a different problem from one toxic level.
miss: Treating severe lithium neurotoxicity with saline alone.
diagramAlt: Lithium interactions. NSAIDs, thiazides, ACE inhibitors raise it Hold the drug. Severe toxicity: dialysis Chronic use: nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

source.name: EXTRIP recommendations for extracorporeal treatment of lithium poisoning.
source.says: The EXTRIP workgroup recommends extracorporeal treatment for severe lithium poisoning.

title: Do not treat tardive dyskinesia with a higher dose as the plan
lead: Tardive dyskinesia is managed by reassessing the antipsychotic, not by raising a first-generation drug. A VMAT2 inhibitor is the specific treatment.
lines: Acute dystonia is the opposite time course and answers to an anticholinergic.
The movements can persist after the drug stops. Warn the patient.
Akathisia is restlessness and is a different dose change.
Acute dystonia is hours and responds to benztropine.
miss: Doubling haloperidol for mouth movements that started after a year of haloperidol.

source.name: StatPearls. Tardive Dyskinesia.
source.says: Tardive dyskinesia is a difficult and potentially chronic adverse effect arising from long-term use of dopamine receptor–blocking medications, most commonly antipsychotic agents.

title: Bell palsy gets a steroid early and eye protection
lead: Idiopathic Bell palsy is treated with oral corticosteroids within the first few days. The eye that does not close is lubricated.
lines: Oral corticosteroids are strongly recommended within 72 hours of onset of peripheral facial nerve palsy.
Antivirals may be added. They are not a substitute for the corticosteroid.
Routine testing is unnecessary for a typical presentation. Atypical features are the reason to test further.
The 2026 facial-nerve-palsy guideline is the source for that 72-hour corticosteroid recommendation.
miss: Starting an antiviral without a corticosteroid, or starting the corticosteroid after 72 hours as if the window were still open.
diagramAlt: Bell palsy, first 72 hours. Forehead involved = peripheral nerve Prednisone early. Lubricate the eye Forehead spared = stroke pathway

source.name: Clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of facial nerve palsy.
source.says: Oral corticosteroids are strongly recommended within 72 hours of symptom onset for peripheral facial nerve palsy. Antivirals may be added. Routine testing is unnecessary for a typical presentation.

title: A deteriorating epidural hematoma goes to surgery
lead: An epidural hematoma in a patient who is worsening goes to surgical evacuation. The lucid interval is the time you still have.
lines: An epidural hematoma larger than 30 mL is evacuated, whatever the Glasgow Coma Scale score.
A patient who was talking and is now worsening does not wait for the next scheduled scan.
Reverse anticoagulation and send a type and screen on the way to the operating room.
The blood is lens-shaped and does not cross sutures. That shape is the middle meningeal artery.

title: Triptan overuse is 10 or more days a month

title: Horner syndrome gets a carotid and an apex

source.says: Acute painful Horner syndrome is imaged for carotid dissection. Vascular imaging is appropriate rather than reassurance.

title: A TIA is a stroke warning, not a cleared patient

The symptoms resolving does not mean the risk resolved.

lead: Spinal cord compression is dexamethasone and urgent decompression or radiation. Plain films are not the test.

title: Do not image ordinary back pain

lead: A gout flare is treated with colchicine, an NSAID, or a glucocorticoid. Allopurinol alone is not the treatment of the flare.

title: Fasciotomy is the treatment of a tight compartment

source.says: Acute compartment syndrome is diagnosed clinically, with pain on passive stretch, and is treated by fasciotomy rather than by more opioid.

title: Inflammatory back pain is treated with an NSAID and movement
lead: Ankylosing spondylitis is treated with an NSAID and with activity. Rest is the wrong prescription.

title: Adult dermatomyositis gets a cancer search

title: Psoriatic arthritis is treated as a joint disease

DIP joints, nail pits, and a whole-digit dactylitis. Rheumatoid arthritis prefers MCP and PIP joints and spares the DIP.

source.says: The clinical manifestations of psoriatic arthritis are varied and can change over time, evolving from one particular pattern to another.

title: Reactive arthritis: treat the germ if it is still there
lead: A persistent triggering infection is treated. The sterile joint itself is treated with an NSAID, not with weeks of unnecessary broad antibiotics.

Uveitis needs an eye exam.
A single dose of antibiotics does not fix established joint inflammation.

title: Marfan syndrome is followed at the aortic root

title: Pemphigus is a steroid disease and the mouth is involved

title: Hip fracture is operated early and protected from clot
lead: A hip fracture in an older adult is operated as soon as the patient is medically ready, generally within a day or two, and is given clot prophylaxis.

lead: HFrEF gets all four: an ARNI, an evidence-based beta blocker, a mineralocorticoid antagonist, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.

title: Bind phosphate with the meal
lead: A phosphate binder is taken with food. A binder swallowed on an empty stomach does not bind the meal the patient is about to eat.
lines: Secondary hyperparathyroidism is treated by lowering phosphate and replacing the vitamin D the kidney no longer activates, in the order the labs demand.
Calcium-based binders add a calcium load. Watch the product.
Dialysis does not excuse the binder.
Phosphate rises, active vitamin D falls, PTH rises. Binders are taken with meals. A bedtime-only dose binds nothing.
miss: Prescribing the binder at bedtime, away from meals.
diagramAlt: Phosphate binder timing. Swallow with the meal Bedtime-only dosing binds nothing Watch the calcium-phosphate product

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD).
source.says: Thus, management of secondary hyperparathyroidism is guided by established surrogate markers of deranged mineral bone metabolism, such as serum calcium, phosphate, PTH, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D.

title: A young woman with fibromuscular stenosis may benefit from opening the artery
lead: Fibromuscular dysplasia of a renal artery in a young woman is the stenosis that is often opened. An older atherosclerotic stenosis is not automatically stented.
lines: An ACE inhibitor can drop the filtration when the whole renal mass sits behind a stenosis.
Recheck the creatinine after you start it.
A bruit is a clue, not a diagnosis.
An ACE inhibitor can drop GFR when both kidneys, or a single kidney, depend on the stenosis. Recheck creatinine within days.
miss: Stenting every atherosclerotic renal artery because the pressure is high.

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Artery Stenosis.
source.says: Renal artery stenosis (RAS) is typically defined as more than 60% narrowing of one or both renal arteries and is a major cause of hypertension, estimated at 1% to 10% of the 50 million people diagnosed with high blood pressure in the United States.

title: Gas in a diabetic kidney is not oral antibiotics
lead: Emphysematous pyelonephritis is treated with antibiotics and a plan to drain or remove the source. It is not a three-day outpatient prescription.
lines: The patient is usually diabetic.
Imaging shows the gas.
A simple pyelonephritis has no gas and can be outpatient if the patient can drink and is not septic.
Gas in the kidney on CT in a diabetic patient is a necrotizing infection, usually E. coli or another gram-negative rod.
Intravenous antibiotics and drainage or nephrectomy. Oral ciprofloxacin and discharge is the miss.
miss: Discharging a febrile diabetic with gas around the kidney on ciprofloxacin.

source.name: StatPearls. Emphysematous Pyelonephritis.
source.says: Emphysematous pyelonephritis (EPN) is a severe necrotizing infection that affects the upper urinary tract, involving the renal parenchyma and, in some instances, the perirenal tissues of the kidney.

title: Minimal change disease in a child is a steroid trial
lead: A child with sudden nephrotic syndrome is treated as minimal change disease with steroids unless a red flag demands a biopsy first.
lines: Hematuria that is heavy, a low complement, or an age outside childhood are reasons not to assume it.
The parents are taught to check the urine and the swelling.
Relapse is common and is not failure of the diagnosis.
Steroids are the first treatment unless hematuria, low complement, or an atypical age demands a biopsy.
miss: Biopsying every edematous toddler before a pediatric nephrologist has seen them.

source.name: StatPearls. Minimal Change Disease.
source.says: Minimal change disease (MCD) is one of the most common causes of idiopathic nephrotic syndrome in children.

title: Membranous nephropathy: look for the cause and the clot
lead: Adult membranous nephropathy is tested for PLA2R antibody, hepatitis, lupus, and cancer, and the nephrotic syndrome is a clot risk.
lines: Anticoagulation is considered when the albumin is very low and the bleeding risk allows it.
Not every patient needs immediate immunosuppression.
A renal-vein thrombosis is flank pain and a worsening kidney, not just more protein.
miss: Starting high-dose steroids on day one and never testing for hepatitis B.

source.name: StatPearls. Membranous Nephropathy.
source.says: Membranous nephropathy (MN), also known as membranous glomerulopathy, is one of the many glomerular diseases causing nephrotic syndrome.

title: Resuscitate the bleed, then scope it
lead: For a stable ulcer bleed without cardiovascular disease, transfuse at a hemoglobin of 7. Scope after resuscitation, within 24 hours.
lines: Two large IVs, a type and screen, and a restrictive transfusion strategy come before the endoscopy.
High-risk stigmata get endoscopic therapy and a proton-pump inhibitor infusion.
A higher transfusion threshold is reasonable for active cardiovascular disease. The number 7 is not universal.
Without cardiovascular disease, transfuse when hemoglobin is under 7 g/dL. Use a higher threshold, often 8, if coronary disease is active.
miss: Transfusing to a hemoglobin of 10 before the scope, or scoping an unstable patient.
diagramAlt: Ulcer bleed transfusion. No heart disease: transfuse under 7 g/dL Scope after resuscitation, within 24 h Higher threshold if active coronary disease

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Upper Gastrointestinal and Ulcer Bleeding.
source.says: A restrictive threshold of 7 g/dL is recommended for patients without cardiovascular disease. Endoscopy follows resuscitation, generally within 24 hours.

title: Tap the new ascites
lead: New ascites gets a diagnostic tap. A SAAG of 1.1 or more means portal hypertension. A neutrophil count of 250 or more means spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.
lines: Send the cell count, albumin, protein, and culture inoculated at the bedside.
Do not wait for the culture to start antibiotics when the neutrophil count is already at least 250.
For a tap that removes more than 5 liters, give albumin, about 6 to 8 g per liter removed.
miss: Sending the patient home on a higher diuretic dose without tapping new or painful ascites.
diagramAlt: Ascites tap. SAAG ≥1.1: portal hypertension Neutrophils ≥250: treat SBP now Remove >5 L: albumin 6–8 g per liter

source.name: AASLD practice guidance. Ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, and hepatorenal syndrome.
source.says: A diagnostic paracentesis is the evaluation of new ascites, and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis is part of what that guidance addresses.

title: The two ulcer causes are H. pylori and NSAIDs
lead: A peptic ulcer is Helicobacter pylori or an NSAID until a rarer cause is proved. The pain’s relation to meals is not reliable enough to locate it.
lines: A clean-based ulcer that has stopped bleeding does not need a heroic transfusion target.
Alarm features, including bleeding, weight loss, and age, get an endoscopy.
Test and treat Helicobacter pylori with a full eradication regimen, then a test of cure. A proton-pump inhibitor alone does not eradicate.
miss: Locating the ulcer from whether food helps, and never testing for H. pylori.
diagramAlt: H. pylori. Full eradication regimen Test of cure after antibiotics PPI alone does not eradicate

source.name: StatPearls. Peptic Ulcer Disease.
source.says: Today, testing for Helicobacter pylori is recommended in all patients with peptic ulcer disease.

title: Reflux is a sphincter that relaxes, not a weak swallow
lead: Gastroesophageal reflux is transient relaxation of the lower sphincter. Dysphagia, bleeding, or weight loss is an alarm, not simple reflux.
lines: A trial of acid suppression is reasonable when the story is heartburn and there is no alarm.
An alarm symptom gets an endoscopy, not a longer antacid trial.
Weight loss and a head of the bed are part of the treatment, not decorations.
Typical heartburn can start with an 8-week proton-pump inhibitor trial. Alarm features — dysphagia, bleeding, anemia, or weight loss — are an endoscopy.
A bird-beak esophagus that does not relax is achalasia, not a failed acid drug. Manometry, not another month of a PPI, is the next test.
miss: Refilling a proton-pump inhibitor for progressive dysphagia.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease.
source.says: Typical reflux symptoms may start with a proton-pump inhibitor trial. Alarm features, including dysphagia, bleeding, anemia, or weight loss, warrant endoscopy rather than another empiric course.

title: Pancreatitis is lipase, gallstones, and alcohol
lead: Acute pancreatitis is epigastric pain to the back with a lipase at least three times normal. Gallstones and alcohol are the two causes to name first.
lines: Two of three: typical pain, lipase at least three times the upper limit, and imaging only if the diagnosis is unclear.
Early fluid is the treatment. Feed when pain allows. Do not trend the lipase every morning.
Antibiotics are not routine for uncomplicated pancreatitis.
miss: Starving the patient for a week because the lipase was high on day one.

source.name: ACG guideline. Management of acute pancreatitis.
source.says: Diagnose acute pancreatitis with two of three: typical pain, lipase or amylase at least three times the upper limit, and imaging when needed. Give early fluid. Do not use routine antibiotics for uncomplicated disease.

title: Small-bowel obstruction stacks air-fluid levels
lead: Small-bowel obstruction is vomiting, distension, and air-fluid levels. Prior surgery means adhesions until a hernia or a mass is found.
lines: A closed loop and a fever or a lactate that is rising is ischemia. That patient does not wait.
Nasogastric suction and fluids are the first orders for a stable partial obstruction.
Complete obstruction with peritonitis is an operation.
Adhesions after surgery are the common cause. Nasogastric suction and fluids if the patient is stable and there is no peritonitis.
miss: Watching a febrile, acidotic obstruction overnight because the last one was adhesions.

source.name: StatPearls. Small Bowel Obstruction.
source.says: Nonoperative management is often effective for partial obstructions, while surgical intervention, such as adhesiolysis or bowel resection, is required in cases of complete obstruction, ischemia, or perforation.

title: Mesenteric ischemia hurts more than the exam shows
lead: Acute mesenteric ischemia is pain out of proportion to the exam. Atrial fibrillation or a low-flow state is the setup, and lactate is late.
lines: The embolus prefers the superior mesenteric artery.
A soft abdomen does not reassure you. The abdomen becomes hard when the bowel is already dead.
CT angiography is the test. A plain film is not.
Pain with a soft abdomen, often atrial fibrillation or low flow. Lactate rises after bowel is injured.
CT angiography and a surgeon now. Heparin if the working diagnosis is embolus and the patient is not bleeding.
miss: Waiting for the lactate or the rigid abdomen before calling the surgeon.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Mesenteric Ischemia.
source.says: Acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI) is a condition due to a sudden decline in blood flow through the mesenteric vessels.

title: Cholecystitis is a blocked cystic duct
lead: Acute cholecystitis is a stone blocking the cystic duct. The pain is right-upper-quadrant and Murphy's sign stops the breath.
lines: Fever and a high white count mark inflammation, not just biliary colic.
Ultrasound shows the wall, the stone, and the fluid.
Early surgery is the treatment of uncomplicated disease. Antibiotics alone do not remove the stone.
Jaundice means the stone may be in the duct. That is a different drainage than removing the gallbladder alone.
miss: Diagnosing cholangitis, which adds jaundice and needs a drained duct, from an isolated gallbladder.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Cholecystitis.
source.says: Chronic and acute pancreatitis can also mimic gallbladder disease.

title: Achalasia is opened or injected, not suppressed with acid medicine
lead: Achalasia is treated by disrupting the lower sphincter: dilation, surgery, or an endoscopic myotomy. A proton-pump inhibitor does not relax it.
lines: Manometry confirms the diagnosis.
Endoscopy excludes a cancer at the junction that mimics the beak.
Aspiration at night is why the treatment is not optional.
Failure of LES relaxation and absent peristalsis. Bird-beak barium. Manometry confirms. Endoscopy excludes a cancer mimic.
miss: Refilling a proton-pump inhibitor for regurgitation of undigested food.

source.name: StatPearls. Achalasia.
source.says: Achalasia represents a disorder of esophageal smooth muscle motility in which the lower esophageal sphincter fails to relax, and peristalsis in the esophageal body is absent.

title: Celiac disease is a gluten-free diet, after the test
lead: Celiac disease is treated by removing gluten. Do the serology and, when needed, the biopsy before the diet, or the tests go negative.
lines: Check total IgA or the test lies.
Dermatitis herpetiformis is the same diet.
A first-degree relative with symptoms is tested. A gene test alone is not the diagnosis.
Order IgA tissue transglutaminase and a total IgA while the patient is still eating gluten. A gluten-free week before the test can make it falsely negative.
HLA-DQ2 or DQ8 is necessary and not sufficient. Adults with a positive serology still need the biopsy before the diet is declared the treatment.
miss: Starting a gluten-free diet the week before the endoscopy.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Celiac Disease.
source.says: Test for celiac disease while the patient is still eating gluten, with IgA tissue transglutaminase and a total IgA. Do not start a gluten-free diet before the test.

title: Severe ulcerative colitis is managed from the current ACG guideline
lead: Severe ulcerative colitis is admitted for steroids and for a watch on toxic megacolon. Antidiarrheals and opioids are stopped.
lines: The 2025 ACG update is the current practice guideline for ulcerative colitis in adults.
A systemically ill patient is assessed under that guideline rather than continued on an unchanged outpatient plan.
Admit, start an intravenous steroid, stop loperamide and opioids, and test for C. difficile. Toxic megacolon is a surgical call.
miss: Sending a systemically ill patient with ulcerative colitis home to continue the outpatient plan.
diagramAlt: Severe ulcerative colitis. Admit. IV steroid Stop loperamide and opioids C. difficile test. Megacolon: call surgery

source.name: ACG clinical guideline update. Ulcerative colitis in adults.
source.says: This is the American College of Gastroenterology's 2025 practice guideline for the management of ulcerative colitis in adults.

title: Chronic pancreatitis enzymes are taken with the meal
lead: Pancreatic enzymes are swallowed with food. A capsule at bedtime does not treat the steatorrhea of the meal.
lines: Diabetes from lost islets is treated as diabetes.
Alcohol is stopped. That is the disease-modifying act.
A new jaundice is cancer until imaged, not more enzymes.
Fecal elastase is low. Enzymes are taken with every meal and snack, not at bedtime alone.
miss: Prescribing the enzymes once daily on an empty stomach.

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Pancreatitis.
source.says: Chronic pancreatitis is a progressive inflammatory disease affecting both pancreatic functions.

title: Varices bleed: drug, antibiotic, band
lead: Suspected variceal bleeding gets a vasoactive drug such as octreotide, an intravenous antibiotic, and urgent endoscopy for banding.
lines: Resuscitate, but do not flood the patient into a higher portal pressure.
Intubation for a massive hematemesis protects the airway before the scope.
Acute variceal bleeding is treated with a vasoactive drug, an antibiotic, and endoscopic therapy. A nonselective beta blocker is prevention after hemostasis, not the treatment of shock.
miss: Starting propranolol while the pressure is 80 and the patient is still vomiting blood.
diagramAlt: Variceal bleed. Octreotide + IV antibiotic Band. Do not start a beta blocker in shock Beta blocker is secondary prevention later

source.name: AASLD Practice Guidance. Portal Hypertensive Bleeding in Cirrhosis.
source.says: Acute variceal bleeding is treated with a vasoactive drug, an antibiotic, and endoscopic therapy. A nonselective beta blocker is prevention after hemostasis, not the treatment of shock, which is the recommendation in AASLD Practice Guidance. Portal Hypertensive Bleeding in Cirrhosis.

title: Chronic hypertension in pregnancy starts at 140/90
lead: Treat chronic hypertension in pregnancy at 140/90. Do not wait for 160/110.
lines: This is the CHAP threshold ACOG adopted. It is a threshold to treat, not a proved ideal target below 140/90.
Continue an effective agent that is safe in pregnancy. Labetalol, nifedipine, and hydralazine are the usual choices.
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and a statin stay stopped.
Treat at 140/90. Labetalol and nifedipine are the usual agents. Stop ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and statins.
miss: Stopping the patient's amlodipine-class plan and watching until the pressure is severe. The error is the wait, and also keeping an ACE inhibitor.
diagramAlt: Blood pressure in pregnancy. Chronic HTN: treat at 140/90 Severe: 160 or 110, treat within minutes Magnesium prevents seizures. It is not the BP drug

source.name: ACOG Practice Advisory. Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP).
source.says: ACOG recommends 140/90 mm Hg as the threshold to start or titrate treatment for chronic hypertension in pregnancy.

title: Severe hypertension in pregnancy is treated now
lead: A sustained pressure of 160 systolic or 110 diastolic in pregnancy or postpartum is treated promptly. Magnesium is for the seizure risk, not for the pressure.
lines: Confirm a severe value and treat. Do not wait four hours, and do not wait for the labs.
IV labetalol, IV hydralazine, or immediate-release oral nifedipine are the acute drugs.
Magnesium sulfate prevents the seizure. It is given with the antihypertensive, not instead of it.
Severe-range blood pressure is treated urgently. Magnesium sulfate is seizure prophylaxis in preeclampsia with severe features.
miss: Starting magnesium and leaving a pressure of 180/115 untreated while the labs are pending.
diagramAlt: Blood pressure in pregnancy. Chronic HTN: treat at 140/90 Severe: 160 or 110, treat within minutes Magnesium prevents seizures. It is not the BP drug

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia.
source.says: Severe-range blood pressure is treated urgently. Magnesium sulfate is seizure prophylaxis in preeclampsia with severe features, which is the recommendation in ACOG Practice Bulletin. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia.

title: Who gets aspirin to prevent preeclampsia
lead: High-risk patients start low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks to lower the risk of preeclampsia.
lines: High risk includes prior preeclampsia, a multifetal pregnancy, chronic hypertension, diabetes, kidney disease, and autoimmune disease.
The dose used in the recommendation is 81 mg daily.
Aspirin does not treat a pressure of 170. That pressure gets an antihypertensive and, if severe features are present, magnesium.
miss: Saving the aspirin for the third trimester, or offering it as the treatment of a pressure of 170/110.

source.name: USPSTF. Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality.
source.says: Low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks is recommended for pregnant people at high risk of preeclampsia.

title: Give insulin in DKA until the gap closes
lead: In diabetic ketoacidosis, continue insulin after the glucose falls and add dextrose. Stop insulin when the gap has closed and the patient is eating, not when the glucose first looks pretty.
lines: The 2024 hyperglycemic-crisis guidance is fluids, potassium, and insulin, and bicarbonate is not routine.
An SGLT2 inhibitor can cause ketoacidosis with a glucose that is not very high. Ask about the drug.
Anion-gap acidosis and ketones. If potassium is under 3.3 mEq/L, replace it before insulin, because insulin will drop the serum potassium.
miss: Turning off the insulin drip because the glucose reached 180 while the bicarbonate is still 10.
diagramAlt: DKA order. Fluid first K under 3.3: replace K before insulin Keep insulin on; add dextrose as glucose falls

source.name: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report.
source.says: Insulin continues until ketoacidosis resolves. Dextrose is added when glucose falls so the insulin can keep running.

title: Thyroid storm: PTU, then iodide an hour later
lead: Thyroid storm treatment starts with propylthiouracil, not iodide. Iodide waits at least 1 hour, a beta blocker and a glucocorticoid are added, and aspirin is avoided. A Burch-Wartofsky score of 45 or more supports the call.
lines: Propylthiouracil is the thionamide preferred in storm because it also blocks conversion of T4 to T3.
Give iodide at least 1 hour after the thionamide. Iodide first supplies substrate for more hormone.
Add a beta blocker and a glucocorticoid. Cool with acetaminophen, not aspirin.
A score of 45 or more supports the diagnosis. A beta blocker alone is not the regimen.
miss: Giving iodide before the thionamide, or using aspirin for the fever.
diagramAlt: Thyroid storm sequence. PTU first. Iodide at least 1 hour later Beta blocker and a glucocorticoid BWPS >=45. No aspirin

source.name: 2016 American Thyroid Association guideline for hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis.
source.says: Thyroid storm, including a Burch-Wartofsky score of 45 or higher, is treated with a beta blocker, propylthiouracil, iodide given at least 1 hour after the thionamide, and a glucocorticoid. Aspirin is avoided.

title: Adrenal crisis is steroid and saline, before the stim test
lead: Adrenal crisis is hydrocortisone and saline now. A cosyntropin test can wait until the patient is alive.
lines: Crisis dose: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV now, then 200 mg over the next 24 hours, with saline.
Do not wait for a corticotropin stimulation test. Recommendation 4.1 treats the unstable patient first.
After recovery, adult maintenance is hydrocortisone 15 to 25 mg a day in divided doses plus fludrocortisone about 0.1 mg.
Send the patient out with stress-dose teaching and a parenteral glucocorticoid for the next emergency.
miss: Holding the glucocorticoid until a stimulation test is finished in an unstable patient.

source.name: Endocrine Society guideline. Primary adrenal insufficiency.
source.says: Recommendation 4.1: adrenal crisis is hydrocortisone 100 mg IV, then 200 mg over 24 hours, plus saline. Do not delay that dose for a corticotropin test. Later maintenance is hydrocortisone 15 to 25 mg a day.

title: Preoperative blockade comes before pheochromocytoma surgery
lead: Prepare a pheochromocytoma with an alpha blocker until the patient is volume-replete, and only then add a beta blocker.
lines: Screen with plasma free metanephrines or urinary fractionated metanephrines. A positive result is followed up, not ignored.
Every patient with a functional tumor gets preoperative blockade before surgery.
Preparation includes a high-sodium diet and a high fluid intake so the blood pressure does not collapse after the tumor is removed.
Block the tumor before incision and load salt and volume so the pressure does not collapse after removal.
miss: Taking a functional pheochromocytoma to surgery without preoperative blockade and volume preparation.

source.name: Endocrine Society guideline. Pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
source.says: All patients with a functional pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma should have preoperative blockade. Preparation includes a high-sodium diet and fluid intake to prevent postoperative hypotension.

title: Pick the diabetes drug for the disease, not the A1C
lead: In type 2 diabetes, start an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven benefit for heart failure, kidney disease, or atherosclerotic disease even when the A1C is already at goal.
lines: Heart failure gets an SGLT2 inhibitor.
Atherosclerotic disease can get a GLP-1 receptor agonist, an SGLT2 inhibitor, or both.
Do not wait through a failed metformin trial when one of those diseases is already present.
Chronic kidney disease is its own reason to choose an SGLT2 inhibitor, even when the A1C is close to goal.
miss: Withholding the drug because the A1C is 6.8.

source.name: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment.
source.says: Agents with proven cardiovascular or kidney benefit are recommended irrespective of A1C when heart failure, chronic kidney disease, or atherosclerotic disease is present.

title: A prolactinoma is a dopamine agonist, after the exclusions
lead: Once pregnancy, hypothyroidism, and drugs are excluded, a prolactinoma is treated with a dopamine agonist.
lines: Cabergoline is the usual drug.
A visual-field cut is an urgent MRI and an urgent treatment, not a routine refill.
Surgery is for the patient who cannot take the drug or whose vision is failing despite it.
Exclude pregnancy, hypothyroidism, and antipsychotics or metoclopramide before calling it a tumor.
A modest elevation with a large mass is stalk effect.
miss: Booking transsphenoidal surgery before a pregnancy test.

source.name: StatPearls. Prolactinoma.
source.says: Hyperprolactinemia is not specific to prolactinoma, and alternative causes such as pregnancy, medications, hypothyroidism, and pituitary stalk effect due to other pituitary tumors should be considered in the differential diagnosis.

title: Endometriosis pain is suppressed, and a large cyst is not
lead: Endometriosis pain is treated with hormonal suppression. A large endometrioma is a surgical lesion, not a longer oral contraceptive alone.
lines: Infertility is managed with the fertility plan, which may not be the same as the pain plan.
NSAIDs help pain and do not treat the implants.
A normal exam does not end the workup of cyclic pain and infertility.
Hormonal suppression treats pain. A cyst of several centimeters is surgical. The fertility plan may differ from the pain plan.
miss: Telling a patient with a 7-centimeter chocolate cyst to try ibuprofen for a year.

source.name: StatPearls. Endometriosis.
source.says: Primary cutaneous endometriosis arises without prior surgery, most frequently affecting the umbilicus, also known as "Villar's nodule." The condition typically manifests as a palpable, discolored skin lesion that may fluctuate in size and symptoms, including pain and bleeding over the affected sites on the skin in response to hormonal changes during the menstrual cycle.

title: A ruptured ectopic pregnancy is an operation
lead: A patient with a positive pregnancy test, an empty uterus, and shock goes to surgery. Methotrexate is for a stable, selected ectopic pregnancy.
lines: The criteria for methotrexate include a low hCG, no fetal heartbeat, and a patient who can return.
Rh status is checked.
A falling hCG still needs a documented plan.
Unstable or ruptured: surgery. Methotrexate only if the patient is stable, the hCG is low, there is no embryonic cardiac activity, and follow-up is certain.
Give anti-D immunoglobulin if the patient is Rh-negative. An empty uterus with a positive test and pain is not a threatened miscarriage until the tube is cleared.
miss: Giving methotrexate in the emergency department to a dizzy patient.
diagramAlt: Ectopic pregnancy. Shock or rupture: operating room Methotrexate only if stable and follow-up is sure Rh-negative: give anti-D

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin. Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy.
source.says: A ruptured or unstable ectopic pregnancy is managed surgically. Methotrexate is reserved for a stable patient who meets criteria and can be followed.

title: Abruption is resuscitation and delivery decisions, not a cervical check
lead: Placental abruption is maternal resuscitation, a fetal monitor, and a delivery decision. Do not perform a digital exam until previa is excluded.
lines: Blood products are ready because the clotting factors are consumed.
A dead fetus and coagulopathy is an urgent delivery.
Painful bleeding is not previa.
Painful bleeding and a uterus that does not relax. Blood can be concealed. Fibrinogen falls and can be the first coagulation test to move.
miss: Checking dilation with a finger as the first act.

source.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 63. Antepartum haemorrhage.
source.says: Placental abruption is painful bleeding and is managed by maternal resuscitation and a prompt delivery decision. Do not perform a digital examination until placenta previa is excluded.

title: Previa is delivered operatively when it covers the cervix
lead: A placenta that covers the cervix is delivered by cesarean. Pelvic rest and a planned date are the outpatient plan after the acute bleed has stopped.
lines: A prior cesarean plus previa raises the chance of placenta accreta. That delivery is planned in a center that can handle it.
The acute bleed is resuscitated like any maternal hemorrhage.
The placenta covers the internal os, so labor and a digital exam can cause hemorrhage. Ultrasound makes the diagnosis.
miss: Inducing labor through a complete previa.

source.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 27a. Placenta praevia and placenta accreta spectrum.
source.says: Diagnose placenta previa with ultrasound and do not perform a digital vaginal examination. Plan cesarean delivery if the placenta still covers the internal os. ACOG Committee Opinion 831 is the US timing document for a medically indicated early delivery.

title: Gestational diabetes is treated to a tight glucose, and the newborn is watched
lead: Gestational diabetes that is not controlled with diet is treated with insulin. The newborn is watched for hypoglycemia.
lines: Gestational diabetes is managed from ACOG Practice Bulletin 190, alongside the current ADA Standards of Care.
After birth, the infant is observed. Maternal glucose has been the fetal fuel.
The mother is retested for diabetes postpartum. Pregnancy treatment is not the end of the diagnosis.
Maternal glucose crosses the placenta and maternal insulin does not. The newborn is hyperinsulinemic, so feed early and check a glucose.
miss: Quoting a glucose cutoff that was not taken from Practice Bulletin 190, or skipping the postpartum retest.
diagramAlt: Infant of a diabetic mother. Glucose crosses. Insulin does not Baby is hyperinsulinemic and can be hypoglycemic Feed early. Check a glucose

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 190. Gestational diabetes mellitus.
source.says: Practice Bulletin 190 is the ACOG management document for gestational diabetes. The PubMed text does not print the diagnostic glucose cutoffs, so this bite does not restate a threshold.

title: Do not combine a nitrate and a PDE-5 inhibitor
lead: If a patient has taken a PDE-5 inhibitor, do not give nitroglycerin. The pressure can collapse.
lines: Ask the question out loud before the first spray.
The wait after sildenafil is longer than after some newer drugs. If you do not know the interval, do not give the nitrate.
Chest pain still gets an ECG and the rest of the ACS plan that is safe.
Sildenafil and a nitrate together can drop systolic pressure profoundly. Ask before the first spray.
If the time of the last dose is unknown, do not give the nitrate. The ECG and aspirin still happen.
miss: Giving the spray because the chest pain protocol says so, without asking.

source.name: ACC/AHA expert consensus. Cardiovascular effects of sildenafil and recommendations for its use.
source.says: Nitrate antianginal agents are an absolute contraindication to sildenafil. Together with nitroglycerin, sildenafil can cause a major drop in blood pressure.

title: BPH is growth in the transition zone
lead: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is proliferation of smooth muscle and epithelial cells in the transition zone. Symptoms become more common with age.
lines: It is a histologic diagnosis, not a nodule and not a rising PSA.
The AUA guideline contains the statements on evaluation and on medical management.
A man with retention, infection, or renal failure is not managed with a sample of one drug.
miss: Promising a man that finasteride will help him urinate tonight.

source.name: AUA guideline. Management of lower urinary tract symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia. Part I.
source.says: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is proliferation of smooth muscle and epithelial cells within the prostatic transition zone, and the guideline covers its evaluation and medical management.

title: Acute scrotal pain is imaged promptly
lead: Acute scrotal pain is an emergency. Ultrasound is the first-line imaging test and is not left until the next morning.
lines: The differential overlaps, so the history alone does not separate torsion from infection.
Ultrasound is the established first-line imaging modality for acute scrotal disease.
A study booked for the following day is not a prompt diagnosis.
miss: Booking a Doppler study for the next available slot in the morning.

title: Rhabdomyolysis is fluids and a potassium you recheck

title: Fat embolism is supported, not anticoagulated as the only plan

title: The four screens and the ages
lead: Mammography starts at 40 and is every other year through 74. Colorectal screening starts at 45. Lung screening is annual low-dose CT from 50 to 80 after 20 pack-years.

miss: Sending a student who cannot explain the risks to get the signature.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Informed consent.
source.says: Informed consent requires disclosure a reasonable patient would want, the patient's understanding, and a voluntary decision. The clinician performing the procedure is responsible for that disclosure, which is the recommendation in AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Informed consent.

title: A sensitive exam uses a chaperone
lead: A breast, pelvic, or genital exam is done with a chaperone offered and, in many settings, present. The patient's comfort is part of consent.
lines: Explain each step before you do it.
A chaperone protects the patient and the clinician.
Stop if consent is withdrawn. An offer that was never made is not a decline.
miss: Proceeding with a pelvic exam after the patient asked you to stop.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 1.2.4, Use of Chaperones.
source.says: AMA Opinion 1.2.4: always honor a patient's request for a chaperone, and use an authorized member of the health care team.

title: Pain medicine at the end of life is not euthanasia
lead: Opioids given to treat pain or air hunger, even if they might hasten death, are not euthanasia when the intent is relief.
lines: Do not withhold morphine from a dying patient because of that confusion.
An opioid dose titrated to pain or air hunger is symptom treatment. The intent is relief, and the dose stops when the symptom stops.
A dose chosen to end life is a different act and is not what this order is. Write the symptom you are treating.
miss: Leaving a dying patient in pain to avoid a theoretical hastening of death.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 5.6, Sedation to Unconsciousness in End-of-Life Care.
source.says: AMA Opinion 5.6: the duty to relieve pain is central, and sedation to unconsciousness must never be used to intentionally cause a patient's death.

title: An impaired colleague is your problem
lead: If a colleague's impairment puts patients at risk, you act. Silence is not loyalty.
lines: Report through the system your institution requires.
A rumor is not the same as an observed impairment. Act on what you know.
Remove the colleague from patients immediately if the impairment is happening now. The report does not wait until the end of the shift.
Review patients already seen. A hallway announcement is not the reporting channel.
miss: Letting an intoxicated colleague finish the shift because confronting them is awkward.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 9.3.2, physician health and wellness, and reporting impaired colleagues.
source.says: An impaired colleague is removed from patient care and reported. A hallway announcement is not the report.

title: Do not alter the record
lead: A late correction is added, dated, and signed. The original note is not deleted or rewritten after a bad outcome.
lines: Changing a note to hide an error is a second harm.
The disclosure to the patient and the note tell the same story.
A correction after a complication is an addendum with the time you learned the fact. The original note stays.
miss: Editing yesterday's note after the complication to make the plan look safer.

source.name: AMA Principles of Medical Ethics, Principle II.
source.says: AMA Principle II: a physician shall be honest in all professional interactions.

title: Research consent is not clinical consent
lead: Enrolling a patient in research requires a research consent that explains the study, the alternatives, and the right to leave. The treatment consent does not cover it.
lines: The patient can decline the study and still receive care.
A power imbalance means you do not pressure.
The consent names what is experimental.
The surgical consent does not enroll the patient. The person obtaining research consent can explain the protocol.
miss: Adding a research biopsy because the patient already signed the surgery consent.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: These events, along with the establishment of the Nuremberg Code and the Declaration of Helsinki, cemented informed consent as a fundamental ethical standard in research and clinical practice.

title: A placebo given as if it were treatment is a deception
lead: Giving a placebo while telling the patient it is an active drug is a deception. It is not a clever therapeutic trial.
lines: If a placebo is studied, the consent says so.
Symptoms still get a real evaluation.
Trust, once broken, ruins the next true recommendation.
Labeling a sugar capsule as an active analgesic is deception. It is not a therapeutic trial.
miss: Prescribing a sugar pill for pain and calling it a strong analgesic.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.4, use of placebo in clinical practice.
source.says: Giving a placebo while telling the patient it is an active drug is a deception. It is not a therapeutic trial.

title: Suspected child abuse is reported without a parent's permission
lead: Suspected child abuse is reported. You do not need the parent's permission, and you do not need proof.
lines: Treat the injury.
The report is to the agency the law names.
A parent who asks you not to report is the reason the duty does not sit with the parent.
Report on suspicion before discharge. A parent's request to keep it private is not a hold. Proof is not the threshold.
Photograph patterned injuries and treat them. Do not discharge to the suspected person while you think about reporting tomorrow.
miss: Agreeing to keep a suspicious fracture between you and the family.
diagramAlt: Report abuse. Suspicion is enough. Proof is not Parent or caregiver cannot veto it Treat the injury and make the report

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 8.10, preventing, identifying, and treating violence and abuse.
source.says: Suspected abuse or neglect is reported. A request to keep it private does not cancel the duty.

title: Organ donation is asked separately from the decision to stop support
lead: The treating team does not couple the request for organs to the moment they recommend stopping support. A designated requester has that conversation.
lines: The decision to stop is the patient's or the surrogate's, made on its own merits.
A conflict of interest is avoided by separating the roles.
The patient who wanted to donate still can. The timing of the ask is what changes.
The decision to stop support is made on its own merits. A designated requester, not the treating team, asks about donation.
miss: Saying you will stop the ventilator if the family agrees to donation.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 6.1.1, organ donation and transplantation.
source.says: The decision to stop support is separate from the request for organ donation, which is made by a designated requester.

title: A POLST is an order. An advance directive is a statement
lead: A POLST or similar portable order tells emergency clinicians what to do tonight. An advance directive tells a surrogate what the patient would have wanted.
lines: They are not interchangeable.
A POLST is a medical order emergency clinicians can follow. An advance directive guides a surrogate and does not travel in an ambulance unless a copy is present.
Reconcile conflicting orders before discharge. A capable patient can void either.
miss: Ignoring a POLST that says do not intubate because an old advance directive was vague.
diagramAlt: POLST versus advance directive. POLST is an order paramedics can follow A directive guides the surrogate A form in a safe does not travel

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Decisions for adult patients who lack capacity.
source.says: When a patient lacks capacity, the surrogate decides by substituted judgment, then by best interest. A written directive that addresses the decision outranks a conflicting surrogate.

title: Against-medical-advice discharge still gets an explanation
lead: A capable patient may leave against advice. You explain the risk, treat what you still can, and document. You do not punish the patient by withholding a prescription they need for a safe exit.
lines: Confirm capacity for this decision.
Offer to treat the dangerous problem before they go.
A signature is not required for you to have had the conversation, and refusal to sign is documented.
A capable patient may leave. Offer the antibiotic or insulin that makes leaving safer. Do not withhold it as a punishment.
miss: Refusing to give a needed antibiotic because the patient is leaving against advice.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.1, Informed Consent.
source.says: AMA Opinion 2.1.1: patients have the right to receive information and ask questions about recommended treatments before they decide.

title: You do not offer a treatment that cannot work
lead: You do not offer a menu of interventions that cannot achieve the patient's goal. Futility is explained, and comfort is offered.
lines: The word is used carefully. A treatment that is unlikely is not the same as one that cannot work.
A second opinion is reasonable. A false hope is not.
The family is not asked to choose among useless options.
Do not offer an intervention that cannot achieve a physiologic goal, such as compressions that cannot restore a circulation.
miss: Asking a family whether they want chest compressions that cannot restore a dead circulation, as if it were a real choice.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 5.5, Medically Ineffective Interventions.
source.says: AMA Opinion 5.5: there is no single definition of futile care. The word depends on the patient's own values and goals.

title: A scarce bed follows a rule you could defend in public
lead: When two patients need one bed or one drug, the rule is clinical and stated in advance. Friendship, fame, and anger do not move the list.
lines: Write the rule before you know the names: acuity, and whether the bed changes the outcome.
A stable patient does not outrank a patient in shock because a colleague called.
If acuity is truly equal, use a tie-break stated in advance. Record that clinical reason in the chart.
The same rule is used on the next shift. Changing it after you see the names is the failure.
miss: Giving the last ICU bed to a colleague's relative who is less sick.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 11.1.3, Allocating Limited Health Care Resources.
source.says: AMA Opinion 11.1.3: a scarce bed is allocated by a policy based on medical need, including urgency and the likelihood and duration of benefit.
